title: Peking University's Talented Female Scholar Wang Li Turns Again: Resigns from AI Entrepreneurship Due to Severe Physical Expenditure, 'People-Oriented' Strikes Industry Pain Points

content_html:
Former Vice President of Research and Safety at OpenAI and co-founder of Thinking Machines Lab, Lilian Weng, recently officially announced her resignation on the social media platform X. This leading figure in the AI safety field, who graduated from Peking University, stated in her farewell letter that she had been unwell more frequently over the past seven months than any other period in her life, and the sustained pressure and workload had exceeded her body's capacity to handle.

From Peking University to the top of Silicon Valley, after seven years of running, she has now pressed the pause button.

Weng had considered switching to a position with a narrower scope of responsibility, but after weighing the options, she believed that "if I cannot fully commit to the work I should be responsible for, it means I have not done this job properly." In her letter, she left a thought-provoking statement: "A future worth building is one that puts people first" — and admitted that she hopes to join an organization with a stable work rhythm and clear responsibilities in the future, no longer taking on the high-pressure pace of a startup as a co-founder.

Mira Murat, the company's founder and CEO, publicly responded to Weng's tweet, acknowledging her choice to prioritize her health and thanking her for all the contributions she made during her tenure. Weng's resume is a benchmark for Chinese scientists in the AI industry: After joining OpenAI in 2018, she started from the robotics team, built and led a safety systems team of more than 80 people, and was deeply involved in the security development of core models such as GPT-4, GPT-4o, and o1. In August 2024, she was promoted to Vice President of Research and Safety at OpenAI, and left in November of the same year.

In February 2025, she co-founded Thinking Machines Lab with former OpenAI CTO Murat and others. The company just completed a $2 billion seed round of financing in July of this year, with a post-money valuation of $12 billion. At a time when the company's valuation was surging, this co-founder chose to step back due to health issues — this twist itself may reveal more about the true nature of the current AI startup scene, which is marked by high valuations, high pressure, and high consumption, than any industry report could.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 前研究与安全副总裁、Thinking Machines Lab 联合创始人 Lilian Weng 近日在社交媒体平台 X 上正式宣布辞职。 这位毕业于北京大学的人工智能安全领域领军人物在告别信中表示，过去七个月里她身体不适的频率比她一生中任何时期都要高，持续的压力和工作量已经超出了她​​身体的承受能力。

从北大到硅谷之巅，七年的奔跑，如今她按下了暂停键。

翁曾考虑过换一个职责范围较小的职位，但权衡之后，她认为“如果我不能全身心地投入到我应该负责的工作中，那就说明我没有做好这份工作”。 她在信中留下了发人深省的一句话：“未来的价值在于以人为本”——并坦言自己希望未来能加入一个工作节奏稳定、职责明确的组织，不再像联合创始人那样承担创业公司的高压节奏。

该公司创始人兼首席执行官米拉·穆拉特(Mira Murat)公开回应了翁的推文，承认她选择优先考虑自己的健康，并感谢她在任职期间做出的所有贡献。 翁的简历是中国人工智能行业科学家的标杆：2018年加入OpenAI后，她从机器人团队开始，建立并领导了80多人的安全系统团队，深度参与了GPT-4、GPT-4o、o1等核心模型的安全开发。 2024年8月，她晋升为OpenAI研究与安全副总裁，并于同年11月离职。

2025年2月，她与前OpenAI CTO Murat等人共同创立了Thinking Machines Lab。 该公司今年7月刚刚完成20亿美元种子轮融资，投后估值为120亿美元。 在公司估值飙升之际，这位联合创始人因健康问题而选择退出——这种转折本身可能比任何行业报告都更能揭示当前人工智能初创公司高估值、高压力、高消耗的真实本质。
